title: Start here
summary: Build one robot, then set it up in three different ways.
need: A Windows 10/11 laptop, your robot kit and a teacher for hardware checks.
result: You know the order of work and which instructions to follow.

title: Check the parts
summary: Find each part and learn its job before connecting anything.
need: The kit laid out on a clear table. Keep cells with the teacher.
result: Every item is accounted for, and missing or damaged parts are reported.

title: Assemble the chassis
summary: Build the base with power off; leave the sensor arrangement easy to change.
need: Chassis, motors, clamps, wheels, caster, boards, holder, screwdriver and teacher-approved fasteners.
result: A stable chassis with clear wheel movement and accessible USB and power switch.

title: Install Arduino on Windows
summary: Prepare the IDE and find the ESP32 USB port.
need: Windows 10/11 laptop, internet for installation, ESP32 and data cable. Battery OFF; external ESP32 5 V lead disconnected.
result: Arduino IDE recognizes a USB COM port and the original ESP32 board target.

title: Upload your first USB test
summary: Prove the laptop can talk to the ESP32 before motors are connected.
need: IDE installed, board/port selected, USB only, motor battery OFF and external 5 V isolated.
result: Sending PING returns PONG at 115200 baud.

title: Wire the base robot
summary: Connect the driver and power path only after the teacher checks the actual modules.
need: USB test passed; battery and USB disconnected; teacher present; readable pin labels.
result: Every base connection is checked against a table before power is applied.

title: Check motor direction & stop
summary: Use short USB commands before letting the robot touch the floor.
need: Base wiring approved; wheels lifted; remote sketch downloaded; teacher-approved test power arrangement.
result: F turns both wheels forward; S and command timeout stop them.

title: Read & calibrate the IR sensors
summary: Measure what LOW and HIGH actually mean on your kit.
need: Teacher-confirmed 3.3 V modules, USB diagnostic power only, motor battery OFF, black/white material and a test obstacle.
result: A recorded raw state for each surface/object and a matching DETECTED_LEVEL setting.

title: Drive from your Windows laptop
summary: Start with short USB commands; then try a Bluetooth Classic COM port.
need: Motor direction and stop tests passed; remote sketch loaded; teacher-approved power setup.
result: You can drive in short movements and reliably stop through the selected serial connection.

title: Set up the line follower
summary: Reposition two sensors and upload the two-sensor program.
need: Base robot tested, IR polarity recorded, two downward mounts, white matte surface and about 25.4 mm black tape.
result: A short supervised test demonstrates steering and a bounded stop.

title: Set up obstacle avoidance
summary: Move three sensors to the sides and front, then test each decision.
need: Base robot tested, three confirmed IR modules, safe matte obstacles, cleared rear space and teacher supervision.
result: The robot chooses a clear side and stops its timed session.

title: Shut down & change modes
summary: End every run with power off and a short test note.
need: The robot in a clear area and the switch reachable.
result: The robot is powered down and ready for safe storage or reconfiguration.

title: Find & fix a problem
summary: Choose the symptom you can observe, then change one thing at a time.
need: Your exact error, sketch name, board/core selection and last successful step.
result: You have an evidence-based next action or a clear report for your teacher.

title: Understand the parts & code
summary: A short reference to read whenever a term is unfamiliar.
need: No practical test required. Use this alongside the setup steps.
result: You can identify the terms and constants used in your sketch.
